name: Client selections
summary: Turns a client's selections (tiles, fittings, colours and other options) into a pack the client chooses from, keeps each choice against its allowance, and chases what is still undecided. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send.

covered_by.allowance-set: intake (the owner records the allowance in the register; the agent reads it)
covered_by.selection-pack-issued: draft (the pack email with the form link is drafted; approval sends it)
covered_by.client-browse: gap (the client browses the booklet or portal themselves)
covered_by.client-chooses: intake (form answers land in the register and are read back)
covered_by.check-against-allowance: gap (no mapped operation compares a choice with its allowance)
covered_by.variation-note: gap (no mapped variation or change order)
covered_by.client-sign-off: gap (no mapped sign-off for a selection)
covered_by.order-item: gap (no mapped supplier order from a selection)
covered_by.chase-undecided: follow-up (chase email for each undecided choice; approval sends it)
covered_by.lead-time-check: gap (no lead-time field in the register or any mapped platform)
covered_by.install-coordinate: gap (no mapped delivery or install scheduling for selections)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Read the selections register, which the client's form answers feed, and keep each row's latest status.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Draft the selection pack email for each row marked Pack ready, then queue its send for approval.

crons.name: follow-up
crons.summary: Queue chase emails for undecided choices once the pack has gone and the chase is due (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reading the register, and creating an email draft in Gmail. Sending a draft reaches the client, so it is a live operation and waits for a person.

google-workspace.covers: selections register in Sheets, selection pack and chase email drafts in Gmail, queued send

gaps: Buildxact: the help centre covers every selection step (allowance items, the client portal, options, client requests, variations, sign-off, record keeping), but its kit folder maps only sign-in. No selection, variation or portal operation exists, so no adapter. Its public REST reference is gated behind a subscription key.
Procore: its help pages do not describe client selections, and the kit has no Procore platform folder, so no adapter.

ProCalc (allowances in the estimate) and Constructive (client portal): no platform folder in the kit, so the allowance and portal steps are the owner's own tools for now. The register holds the allowance values the owner types in.
Google Form: the form itself is not mapped. Its answers are read from the linked sheet through the register, so the form must keep writing to the register's columns.
Client browsing and choosing happen in the client's own booklet or portal. The agent cannot see what the client looked at, only what they chose.
Allowance comparison, variation or change order, sign-off, supplier ordering, lead times and installation scheduling have no mapped operation on any platform in the evidence. Each is a person's step.
Judgment steps (answering a client's question from the booklet, deciding whether a request is an extra that needs a variation, choosing the chase tone) belong to the agent skill, not the crons.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox Google Workspace account proves it. Its platform status is spec, tested offline only.
A rejected pack is not queued again: a person redoes it by hand.
